conviction_note: The evidence points both ways and nets to about zero. Peers that reported after MMYT last spoke point up on hotels and bus: IHCL raised its FY27 guide, ixigo bus GTV rose 32%. Industry air volumes in Jul-Aug were worse than in Q1 and oil went back above $100 in Sep-Oct, which points down on air and on the outlook. Management already flagged a soft domestic-air quarter on Aug 3. So p_up sits at 51 on a 9.5% abs move (real prints moved -5%, about -8 to -12%, about -8 to -12%, +8.5%). The findings sum to +0.5 against a scaled +0.19; that gap is just the near-balance, not a disagreement.
bar: Revenue consensus is $267.4M (Investing.com, 2026-10-23, https://uk.investing.com/news/stock-market-news/makemytrip-earnings-on-deck-as-india-travel-faces-fuel-headwinds-93CH-4928927) and $269.09M (MarketBeat, 2026-10-19, https://www.marketbeat.com/instant-alerts/upcoming-makemytrip-mmyt-expected-to-post-quarterly-earnings-on-monday-2026-10-19/). The two sources agree. That bar implies about +17% reported growth against Q2 FY26's $229.3M, which needs about +25-28% constant currency with the rupee down about 9% YoY, against Q1 FY27's +16.1% cc. The same vendor consensus overshot Q2 FY26 revenue by 13.2% (Zacks, https://finance.yahoo.com/news/makemytrip-mmyt-q2-earnings-revenues-122502393.html), so it looks mis-specified. EPS consensus is $0.03-0.04, which reads as an IFRS-basis figure: Q1 printed $0.53 adjusted against a $0.22 'consensus'. That makes the EPS bar disputed. The stock trades on gross bookings, adjusted margin and adjusted operating profit (Q1: 1.8% of gross bookings, which management guided to stay 'around 1.8%'), and no sourced consensus exists for those. print_vs_bar_pct is measured against the $268M revenue bar and assumes about 16% cc growth less 9 points of FX, roughly $245-250M. Findings that depend on the revenue bar are capped small.
positioning_check: Short interest was 8,233,580 shares on the 2026-09-30 record date, 9.76% of float, 8.5 days to cover, up 3.5% from 7.96M (MarketBeat, https://www.marketbeat.com/stocks/NASDAQ/MMYT/short-interest/). An aggregator snippet gave about 9.0M shares and 12.3 days to cover on 2026-08-14 (https://curvedtrading.com/stocks/mmyt/short-interest/, snippet_only, page 403). Part of this is probably convertible-arbitrage hedging against about $1.6B of convertible notes, so not all of it is a directional short. Even so, it is moderately crowded, which shrinks the negatives. The skew is +6.56 vol points (downside paid) and put/call OI is 9.27, but total OI is only 1,161 and the ATM spread is 60% of mid, so the option lean is indicative only. The stock is down 52% from its 52-week high, -8% over 20 days and -7.7% over 5 days, and trades below its 50-day average of $52.08. Hedge-fund holders fell from 26 to 14 over Q2 (Insider Monkey, 2026-10-08).

findings.finding: Industry domestic air volume weakened through the reported quarter, more than in Q1. DGCA/ICRA put July 2026 at 12.0M passengers (-4.8% YoY, capacity -7.8%) and August at 12.126M (-6.34% YoY), against April's -2.0%. On the Aug 3 call management said the seasonal domestic-air drop 'could be larger than usual' and declined to commit to 20%+ cc growth. BofA expects 'a soft 2Q'. Air ticketing was 32% of Q1 adjusted margin and grew only +10.8% cc there.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q4 FY26 (2026-05-19): an air/international deceleration and a cautious outlook sold off about -7.7% to -12%. Q1 FY27 (2026-08-03): air was the weak segment but total bookings beat a low bar, and the stock rose about +8.5%.
findings.why_not_priced: This is mostly priced. The data is public, management telegraphed it and BofA previewed a soft Q2. What is not visible is the size of the hit to MMYT's air segment: no air-segment consensus is published. If the market had fully priced a worse-than-Q1 air quarter, the revenue consensus would not sit at an implied +17% reported. The rest of the company (hotels and packages 43%, bus 17%, others 8% of adjusted margin) grew 21-32% cc in Q1 and has positive peer reads (see the IHCL and ixigo bus findings), so this is sized net of that.
findings.independence: Management call summary, Aug 2026: https://www.webull.com/news/15378440584635392. BofA preview quoted by Investing.com, 2026-10-23: https://uk.investing.com/news/stock-market-news/makemytrip-earnings-on-deck-as-india-travel-faces-fuel-headwinds-93CH-4928927

findings.finding: Indian Hotels (IHCL) reported Q2 FY27 on 2026-10-21, after MMYT's last print. Consolidated revenue rose 21% YoY and standalone revenue 26%. Search-snippet summaries put domestic same-store RevPAR at about +25%. IHCL raised its FY27 revenue-growth guide from 12-14% to 15-17%. That points to strong domestic hotel demand in Jul-Sep for MMYT's hotels and packages segment, its largest at 43% of Q1 adjusted margin and +21.3% cc in Q1.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q1 FY27: hotels and packages +21.3% cc carried a bookings beat, and the stock rose about +8.5%.
findings.why_not_priced: MMYT fell about 7.7% in the five sessions that include this release, so the ADR has not traded on the read-through. If it had, the stock would not be making new lows into the print with downside skew bid. This is a proxy: IHCL is luxury and upper-upscale, and MMYT's hotels line includes weak outbound packages, so it is sized small.
findings.independence: ixigo Q2 FY27 (2026-10-17) hotel GTV +159% and room nights +295%, a different document (https://inc42.com/buzz/ixigo-swings-to-₹63-cr-profit-in-q2-revenue-rises-13-yoy/), though from a tiny base.

findings.finding: ixigo (Le Travenues) reported Q2 FY27 on 2026-10-17: bus GTV rose 31.6% YoY to ₹752.7 Cr, passengers +28% and bus revenue +23.8%. ixigo attributed part of that to high airfares pushing intercity travellers to buses. That is a direct counterparty read for MMYT's redBus segment, 17% of Q1 adjusted margin and +32.4% cc in Q1.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Bus has been MMYT's fastest-growing segment (Q1 FY27 +32.4% cc). No resolved print where bus alone drove the reaction.
findings.why_not_priced: ixigo is an NSE-listed peer that few US ADR holders follow. The read-through is substitution: high airfares push travellers to buses, which offsets part of the air weakness inside MMYT. The ADR fell on the week rather than rising on it. The segment is small, so it is sized small.
findings.independence: Same document as the ixigo flights finding below. Upstox, 2026-10-19, confirms bus GTV +32%: https://upstox.com/news/market-news/stocks/ixigo-shares-rally-15-as-revenue-soars-13-yo-y-to-321-crore-hotel-gtv-grows-2-6x-check-q2-results/article-202068/

findings.finding: ixigo's Q2 FY27 flights business grew GTV +37.2% and passengers +8%, against an industry domestic market down about 5-6%. Its flight take rate fell from 9.38% to 7% and flight revenue fell 7.5%. Fare inflation is lifting GTV while monetisation compresses, and a smaller rival is buying air share. Both are negative reads for MMYT's air adjusted margin per booking and its air share.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q3 FY26 (2026-01-21) revenue missed and the stock fell about -8% intraday to -12% close-to-close. Q4 FY26 sold off on air/international deceleration.
findings.why_not_priced: ixigo's segment take rate is buried in an Indian peer's release. The ADR consensus has no air take-rate line, and BofA's preview frames the problem as supply and volume, not monetisation. ixigo's take-rate fall may be ixigo-specific discounting rather than an airline commission change, so it is sized small.
findings.independence: Same ixigo document as the bus finding (two readings of one release, opposite segments, so no double count). Industry volume: https://www.angelone.in/news/economy/india-s-domestic-air-traffic-drops-6-34-to-12-126-million-passengers-in-august-2026

findings.finding: The setup into the print has a low bar. The stock is down 52% from its high, -7.7% over 5 days and below its $52.08 50-day average. Short interest is 9.76% of float with 8.5 days to cover (2026-09-30, up 3.5%), and hedge-fund holders fell from 26 to 14. The last time the bar was this washed out (Q1 FY27, analysts reportedly at about 3% GBV growth), MMYT printed +19.9% cc bookings and rose about +8.5%.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q1 FY27 (2026-08-03): a low bar plus a bookings beat gave about +8.5%, helped by an Iran-deal sector rally.
findings.why_not_priced: Positioning is the baseline to beat, not hidden information. Some of the short interest is convertible-arbitrage hedging, which will not squeeze. The downside skew, though illiquid, says the option market leans the other way. Sized small for those reasons.
findings.independence: Hedge-fund holder count: https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/disruption-middle-east-weighed-makemytrip-131304926.html (2026-10-08). The Q1 low bar is a snippet only, from a search result citing an unnamed firm.

findings.finding: Oil re-escalated late in the reported quarter and is still high going into the print. Brent passed $100 on 2026-09-09 for the first time since July (HSBC raised its 2026 forecast to $90, Hormuz flows about 6-10M bpd against 19-20M pre-war) and stood about $107-110 in mid-October. Management's Aug 3 optimism rested on oil having fallen after an MOU, so the Q3 (festive season) commentary on airfares, airline capacity and outbound will probably stay cautious.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q4 FY26 (2026-05-19): a cautious West Asia outlook drove about -7.7% to -12%. MMYT gives no formal guidance, so the outlook commentary is the guide.
findings.why_not_priced: This is largely priced. The stock fell from about $52 to $43 as oil rose, and the Artisan letter blames the Middle East. What is unpriced is only whether management quantifies a festive-quarter slowdown. This is macro-to-company transmission the company has not confirmed since August, so it is sized small.
findings.independence: Mid-October Brent about $107-110 (Economie Matin citing Reuters, 2026-10-19): https://www.economiematin.fr/?p=234386. Management's Aug 3 framing that demand recovered after oil fell: https://www.webull.com/news/15378440584635392

findings.finding: The headline revenue line is set up to 'miss'. Consensus of $267-269M implies +17% reported, or about +25-28% cc with the rupee down about 9% YoY, against Q1 FY27's +16.1% cc. A Q1-like quarter prints about $245-250M, roughly 8% below the bar. The same vendor consensus overshot Q2 FY26 by 13.2% ($229.3M actual).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q3 FY26 (2026-01-21): revenue $295.7M against $304.1M FactSet, -8% to -12%. Q1 FY27: revenue 'miss' but the stock rose about +8.5% on bookings and profit. Q2 FY26: a 13.2% revenue miss (reaction not established).

findings.why_not_priced: Holders know the aggregated revenue consensus is unreliable on this name, so a headline miss is partly expected. It can still drive the first algorithmic and pre-market reaction, as in January. The bar is mis-specified, so this is capped small.

findings.finding: MakeMyTrip (India) Ltd confidentially pre-filed a DRHP with SEBI/BSE/NSE on 2026-07-17. It is expected to be an offer for sale by MMYT and ibibo, with proceeds earmarked for cash, inorganic growth and 'repurchases of securities, including convertibles'. Media reports put the deal above $1B. MMYT repurchased $7.8M in Q1. A timeline or valuation update on the Q2 call would show listed Indian OTA multiples against a $4.1B ADR.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior print turned on the IPO. The July 17 filing day was not a large move (baseline 6-K row +0.77%, a text-match day, not a print).
findings.why_not_priced: The filing is public. What is not public is whether the call adds a timing or valuation update. The ADR at -52% from its high suggests no IPO-unlock value is in the price. Whether it surfaces inside the window is uncertain, so it is sized near zero.
findings.independence: Q1 call: $7.8M buyback, IPO proceeds for convertible redemption or repurchase (https://www.webull.com/news/15378440584635392). Media size reports: https://www.angelone.in/news/ipos/makemytrip-ipo-travel-platform-is-reportedly-eyeing-a-1-billion-listing-in-india

findings.why_not_priced: It is guided, so it is priced by construction. It sits near zero, inside the guided range.
